newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate panel to vote on revised reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate panel to vote on revised reform bill.

text.p: The Brazilian government's pension reform bill may come up for a vote by a Senate panel later this week after members of the upper house reached a compromise on a sticking point, a senator in charge of the bill said Tuesday.

Sen. Beni Veras said an accord had been struck on a "parity" article of the bill, which would have prevented public sector pensioners from gaining immediate increases to match pay rises given to workers.
Under the agreement, retirees receiving pensions of up to 10 minimum salaries -- 1,200 reais, or $1,111 -- will be entitled to any pay increase given to workers, Veras said.
The increases for pensioners receiving more than 10 minimum salaries would be gradually reduced to a minimum of 70 percent of the value of raises given to workers, he said.

Asked whether the proposal represented a dilution of the government's intention of cutting pension perks for civil servants, Veras said it was a "consensus" agreement that would pave the way for progress on the reform bill.

The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee could vote on the bill on Thursday. If approved the legislation would advance to the floor of the Senate, where it must secure three-fifths majorities in two separate ballots.
The reform bill, which has been in Congress for more than two years, must also return to the Chamber of Deputies for approval of changes made in the Senate.
